paper.title: Adaptive Algorithms for Relaxed Pareto Set Identification

settings.name_in_paper: eps_1-PSI-k (fixed-confidence relaxed Pareto set identification, at most k Pareto optimal arms)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued, D-dimensional) rewards; Pareto set identification.
unmapped: Arms are distributions over R^D (D objectives) with 1-subgaussian marginals
Correct answer: either k arms all in the eps_1-Pareto set, or fewer than k arms containing the Pareto set and contained in the eps_1-Pareto set
Learner knows the number of objectives D, the slack eps_1 and the target number k
settings.definition_quote: $\hat S \subset \bA$ is correct for $\eps_1$-{PSI}-$k$ if either \emph{i)} $\lvert \hat S\lvert = k$ and $\hat S \subset \cS^\star_{\eps_1}$ or \emph{ii)} $ \lvert \hat S\lvert <k$ and $\cS^\star \subset \hat S \subset \cS^\star_{\eps_1}$ holds.

settings.name_in_paper: (eps_1, eps_2)-PSI (identification of an (eps_1,eps_2)-cover of the Pareto set)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued, D-dimensional) rewards; Pareto set identification.
unmapped: Arms are distributions over R^D with 1-subgaussian marginals
Correct answer is an (eps_1, eps_2)-cover of the Pareto set
settings.definition_quote: A subset $S\subset \bA$ is an $(\eps_1, \eps_2)$-cover of the \emph{Pareto set} if : $S\subset \cS^\star_{\eps_1}$ and for any $i\notin S$ either $i\notin \cS^\star$ or $\exists j \in S$ such that $\vmu_i \prec \vmu_j + {\eps_2}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Best Arm Identification (D=1 special case of PSI)
settings.definition_quote: Let $\delta \in (0, 1), K\geq 2$ and $\nu$ a $K-$armed bandit with a unique best arm $a_\star$ and $1$-subgaussian distributions.

algorithms.name: eps_1-APE-k (Adaptive Pareto Exploration with stopping rule tau_{eps_1}^k, pairwise mixture-martingale confidence bonuses)
APE with LUCB1-like single-arm confidence bonuses and stopping time tau_{eps_1}^k

symbols.Delta_tilde_i: max(Delta_i, eps_1, omega^k) with Delta_i the Pareto sub-optimality gap of arm i and omega^k the k-th largest omega_i = min_{j != i} M(i,j)
symbols.D_obj: number of objectives (dimension of the reward vectors)
symbols.k: maximal number of Pareto optimal arms to return

tuning: confidence bonus beta_{i,j}(t) of eq. (beta) with K_1 = K(K-1)D/2

source.label: thm:sampcompl
source.quote: Fix a risk parameter $\delta \in (0, 1)$, $\eps_1\geq 0$, let $k\leq K$ and $\nu$ a bandit with $1$-subgaussian marginals. With probability at least $1 - \delta$, $\eps_1$-{APE}-$k$ recommends a correct set for the $\eps_1$-{PSI}-$k$ objective and stops after at most \sum_{a \in \bA} \frac{88}{{\widetilde\Delta_a}^2}\log(...) samples, where for each $a\in \bA$, $\widetilde{\Delta}_a := \max(\Delta_a, \eps_1,\omega^k)$.

results.notes: With k=K this gives an eps_1-PSI guarantee. Paper's Delta_i is a Pareto gap, not mu_star - mu_i, hence declared Delta_tilde_i. Per-round cost O(K^2 D).

symbols.Delta_k_i: Delta_i + omega^k (Pareto gap plus k-th largest omega)

conditions: exists a bandit instance (multivariate Gaussian with identity covariance) with |S*| = p >= 3

source.quote: There exists a bandit instance $\nu$ with $\lvert \cS^\star \lvert = p\geq 3$ such that for $k \in \{ p, p-1, p-2\} $ any $\delta$-correct algorithm for $0$-PSI-$k$ verifies \[ \bE_\nu(\tau_\delta) \geq \frac{1}{D} \log\left(\frac1\delta\right) \sum_{a=1}^K\frac{1}{(\Delta_a^k)^2},\] where $\Delta_a^k := \Delta_a + \omega^k$

results.notes: Existential (worst-case instance) lower bound; in the construction all arms are Pareto optimal (p = K).

tuning: beta_i(t) = sqrt(2/T_i(t) * log(5 K D t^4/(2 delta))), beta_{i,j} = beta_i + beta_j

source.quote: Let $\eps_1 \geq 0, k\leq K$ and $\nu$ a bandit with $1$-subgaussian marginals. \algname run with the $\beta_i'$s of \eqref{eq:beta-single} and associated to the stopping time $\tau_{\eps_1}^k$ outputs a valid set and its expected sample complexity is upper-bounded as follows : $$ \bE_{\nu}(\tau_{\eps_1}^k) \leq {64\sqrt e H}\log\left( \frac{5KD}{2\delta}\right) + {256\sqrt e H}\log\left({256H}\right) + \frac{8\pi^2}{15} + 1,$$

results.notes: Bound on E[tau] (not restricted to the good event).

symbols.Delta_eps_i: max(Delta_i, eps_1) with Delta_i the Pareto gap

source.label: thm:sampcompl2
source.quote: Fix $\delta \in (0, 1)$, $\eps_1, \eps_2 \geq 0$. Then $(\eps_1, \eps_2)$-\algname outputs an $(\eps_1, \eps_2)$-cover of the {Pareto set} with probability at least $1-\delta$ using at most \sum_{a \in \bA} \frac{88}{(\Delta_a^{\eps})^2} \log(...) samples, where for all $a\in \bA$, $\Delta_a^{\eps} := \max(\Delta_a, \eps_1)$.

results.notes: Printed number per annotation is Theorem 1 (appendix counter).

source.label: thm:sampl_compl_BAI
source.quote: Let $\delta \in (0, 1), K\geq 2$ and $\nu$ a $K-$armed bandit with a unique best arm $a_\star$ and $1$-subgaussian distributions. \algname associated to be stopping time $\tau_0^1$ identifies the best arm $a^\star$ with probability at least $1-\delta$ using at most the following number of samples \[ \sum_{a=1}^K \frac{88}{\Delta_a^2} \log\left(\frac{2K(K-1)}\delta \log\left(\frac{12e}{\Delta_{a}}\right)\right). \]

results.notes: Delta of the best arm is the minimum gap Delta_min (classical BAI convention).

cited_results.cited_title: Pareto front identification from stochastic bandit feedback
cited_results.setting_description: eps_1-PSI, fixed-confidence Pareto set identification with sub-Gaussian marginals; sample complexity scales as a sum over arms of 1/(Delta_i v eps_1)^2 (up to logs)
